claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Bray, 2006; Artavanis-Tsakonas and Muskavitch, 2010).

claims.claim: A zone of Notch signaling is established between the dorsal and ventral halves of the Drosophila wing imaginal disc.
claims.source: For example, a zone of Notch signaling is established between the dorsal and ventral halves of the Drosophila wing imaginal disc (Baker, 2007).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Baker, 2007).

claims.claim: Fringe proteins modify Notch receptors and ligands to increase the level of Notch signaling by Delta ligands and to attenuate Notch signaling by Serrate ligands.
claims.source: Fringe proteins modify Notch receptors and ligands to increase the level of Notch signaling by Delta ligands and to attenuate Notch signaling by Serrate ligands (Rana and Haltiwanger, 2011; LeBon et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Rana and Haltiwanger, 2011; LeBon et al., 2014).

claims.claim: Fringe modification of Notch receptors tends to enhance signaling by Dll1 and Dll4 ligands and attenuate signaling by Jag1 and Jag2.
claims.source: Current evidence suggests that Fringe modification of Notch receptors tends to enhance signaling by Dll1 and Dll4 ligands and attenuate signaling by Jag1 and Jag2 (Hicks et al., 2000; LeBon et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Hicks et al., 2000; LeBon et al., 2014).

claims.claim: Differentiating hair cells express three Notch ligands: Dll1, Dll3 and Jag2.
claims.source: Differentiating hair cells express three Notch ligands, Dll1, Dll3 and Jag2 (Lanford et al., 1999; Morrison et al., 1999; Hartman et al., 2007; Maass et al., 2015), of which Dll1 and Jag2 act as conventional Notch ligands, whereas Dll3 appears to act only by inhibiting Notch receptors in the same cell (Ladi et al., 2005; Geffers et al., 2007; Chapman et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Lanford et al., 1999; Morrison et al., 1999; Hartman et al., 2007; Maass et al., 2015).

claims.claim: Dll1 and Jag2 act as conventional Notch ligands.
claims.source: Differentiating hair cells express three Notch ligands, Dll1, Dll3 and Jag2 (Lanford et al., 1999; Morrison et al., 1999; Hartman et al., 2007; Maass et al., 2015), of which Dll1 and Jag2 act as conventional Notch ligands, whereas Dll3 appears to act only by inhibiting Notch receptors in the same cell (Ladi et al., 2005; Geffers et al., 2007; Chapman et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: Dll3 appears to act only by inhibiting Notch receptors in the same cell.
claims.source: Differentiating hair cells express three Notch ligands, Dll1, Dll3 and Jag2 (Lanford et al., 1999; Morrison et al., 1999; Hartman et al., 2007; Maass et al., 2015), of which Dll1 and Jag2 act as conventional Notch ligands, whereas Dll3 appears to act only by inhibiting Notch receptors in the same cell (Ladi et al., 2005; Geffers et al., 2007; Chapman et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Ladi et al., 2005; Geffers et al., 2007; Chapman et al., 2011).

claims.claim: Notch signaling controls two sets of decisions at the edge of the organ of Corti.
claims.source: We find Notch signaling controls two sets of decisions at the edge of the organ of Corti.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the authors' experimental findings and interpretation.

claims.claim: The first decision restricts the first differentiating inner hair cells and their associated supporting cells, the inner phalangeal cells, to the boundary with Kölliker's organ.
claims.source: The first decision restricts the first differentiating inner hair cells and their associated supporting cells, the inner phalangeal cells, to the boundary with Kölliker's organ.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the authors' experimental findings and interpretation.

claims.claim: The first fate decision is regulated by Fringe activity, requires low levels of Notch signaling and is extremely sensitive to changes in signaling strength.
claims.source: We find this fate decision is regulated by Fringe activity, requires low levels of Notch signaling and is extremely sensitive to changes in signaling strength.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the authors' experimental findings and interpretation.

claims.claim: The second decision regulates the proportion of hair cells and supporting cells through lateral inhibition.
claims.source: The second decision regulates the proportion of hair cells and supporting cells through previously characterized forms of lateral inhibition (Lewis, 1991, 1998; Kiernan, 2013).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the authors' experimental findings, interpretation, and citations to previous studies (Lewis, 1991, 1998; Kiernan, 2013).

claims.claim: The second fate decision does not require Fringe activity, requires higher levels of Notch signaling, and is much less sensitive to small changes in signaling strength.
claims.source: This fate decision does not require Fringe activity, requires higher levels of Notch signaling, and is much less sensitive to small changes in signaling strength.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the authors' experimental findings and interpretation.

claims.claim: Qualitatively different forms of Notch signaling regulate different fate decisions during organ of Corti development.
claims.source: Our results suggest that qualitatively different forms of Notch signaling regulate different fate decisions during organ of Corti development.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the authors' experimental findings and interpretation.

claims.claim: Lfng and Mfng are transiently expressed precisely at the neural boundary of the organ of Corti.
claims.source: We show that two Notch modifiers, Lfng and Mfng, are transiently expressed precisely at the neural boundary of the organ of Corti.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the authors' in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1.

claims.claim: The region where Lfng and Mfng are transiently expressed gives rise to inner hair cells and their associated inner phalangeal cells.
claims.source: Cre-Lox fate mapping shows this region gives rise to inner hair cells and their associated inner phalangeal cells.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by fate mapping data shown in Figure 2.

claims.claim: Mutation of Lfng and Mfng disrupts the boundary of the organ of Corti, producing unexpected duplications of inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells.
claims.source: Mutation of Lfng and Mfng disrupts this boundary, producing unexpected duplications of inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by data from Lfng;Mfng double mutant mice shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claims.claim: The duplication phenotype is mimicked by other mouse mutants or pharmacological treatments that lower but not abolish Notch signaling.
claims.source: This phenotype is mimicked by other mouse mutants or pharmacological treatments that lower but not abolish Notch signaling.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by data from multiple mutants and culture experiments shown in Figures 3 and 5.

claims.claim: Strong disruption of Notch signaling generates many ectopic hair cells at the expense of inner phalangeal cells.
claims.source: However, strong disruption of Notch signaling causes a very different result, generating many ectopic hair cells at the expense of inner phalangeal cells.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by data from Notch1 conditional mutants and high-dose inhibitor treatments shown in Figures 3 and 5.

claims.claim: Notch signaling is finely calibrated in the cochlea to produce precisely tuned levels of signaling that first set the boundary of the organ of Corti and later regulate hair cell development.
claims.source: Our results show that Notch signaling is finely calibrated in the cochlea to produce precisely tuned levels of signaling that first set the boundary of the organ of Corti and later regulate hair cell development.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the authors' experimental findings and interpretation.

claims.claim: Pofut1 is an O-fucosyltransferase that adds fucose moieties to Notch receptors and ligands.
claims.source: Pofut1 is an O-fucosyltransferase that adds fucose moieties to Notch receptors and ligands (Takeuchi and Haltiwanger, 2010), and whose activity generates the O-fucose substrate that is necessary for further N-glycosylation of Notch receptors by Fringe proteins (Shi and Stanley, 2003; Shi et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Takeuchi and Haltiwanger, 2010).

claims.claim: Pofut1 activity generates the O-fucose substrate that is necessary for further N-glycosylation of Notch receptors by Fringe proteins.
claims.source: Pofut1 is an O-fucosyltransferase that adds fucose moieties to Notch receptors and ligands (Takeuchi and Haltiwanger, 2010), and whose activity generates the O-fucose substrate that is necessary for further N-glycosylation of Notch receptors by Fringe proteins (Shi and Stanley, 2003; Shi et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Shi and Stanley, 2003; Shi et al., 2005).

claims.claim: Pofut1 null mutant mice die between E9.5 and E10.5 with an axial phenotype reminiscent of a Notch loss of function.
claims.source: Pofut1 null mutant mice die between E9.5 and E10.5 with an axial phenotype reminiscent of a Notch loss of function (Shi and Stanley, 2003), although different tissues can display differential sensitivities to loss of Pofut1 (Schuster-Gossler et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Shi and Stanley, 2003; Schuster-Gossler et al., 2009).

claims.claim: Conditional deletion of Pofut1 in the cochlea with Pax2-Cre transgenic mice leads to a reduction, but not a complete loss of Notch signaling.
claims.source: Conditional deletion of Pofut1 in the cochlea with Pax2-Cre transgenic mice leads to a reduction, but not a complete loss of Notch signaling, as revealed by the presence of cleaved Notch1-intracellular protein in the nuclei of Pofut1 mutant supporting cells and the enhancement of the Pofut1 mutant phenotype by additional Notch inhibition with gamma secretase inhibitors in organ culture (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and culture data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claims.claim: Loss of Lfng alone is able to rescue the inner hair cell phenotype, but not the outer hair cell phenotype of Jag2 mutant mice.
claims.source: Our model can also explain why mutation of Lfng alone is able to rescue the inner hair cell phenotype, but not the outer hair cell phenotype of Jag2 mutant mice (Zhang et al., 2000).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Zhang et al., 2000).

claims.claim: Loss of Lfng would partially relieve cis-inhibition of Dll1 expressed at the boundary and allow it to deliver more Notch signal to compensate for the loss of Jag2.
claims.source: Since Lfng normally enhances cis-inhibition between Delta ligands and Notch receptors expressed in the same cell (LeBon et al., 2014), we predict that loss of Lfng would partially relieve cis-inhibition of Dll1 expressed at the boundary and allow it to deliver more Notch signal to compensate for the loss of Jag2.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from the known function of Lfng and a citation (LeBon et al., 2014).

claims.claim: An interaction between Lfng, Rfng and Mfng has been observed in the maturation of marginal zone B cell precursors.
claims.source: However, an interaction between Lfng, Rfng and Mfng has been observed in the maturation of marginal zone B cell precursors (Tan et al., 2009; Song et al., 2016), suggesting that in at least some cases, the combined effects of these three enzymes on Notch signaling in either cis or trans cannot be achieved by either alone.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Tan et al., 2009; Song et al., 2016).

claims.claim: A previous study described significant increases in proliferation in the progenitors of pillar cells, Deiters' cells and Hensen's cells in Dll1+/−;Jag2−/− and Dll1hyp/−;Jag2−/− mutant embryos, but not single mutants for either ligand.
claims.source: A previous study described significant increases in proliferation in the progenitors of pillar cells, Deiters' cells and Hensen's cells in Dll1+/−;Jag2−/− and Dll1hyp/−;Jag2−/− mutant embryos, but not single mutants for either ligand (Kiernan et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Kiernan et al., 2005).

claims.claim: The strength of Notch signaling in vertebrates can vary according to both the identity and post-translational modification of the activated Notch receptor and the identity of the activating ligand.
claims.source: It is now well established that the strength of Notch signaling in vertebrates can vary according to both the identity and post-translational modification of the activated Notch receptor and the identity of the activating ligand (for example, Ong et al., 2006; Yamamoto et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2013; Van de Walle et al., 2013; LeBon et al., 2014; Petrovic et al., 2014; Gama-Norton et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claims.claim: Hes5 mutant mice develop supernumerary inner hair cells and supporting cells at the onset of hair cell differentiation.
claims.source: Furthermore, Hes5 mutant mice develop supernumerary inner hair cells and supporting cells at the onset of hair cell differentiation (Zine et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Zine et al., 2001).

claims.claim: Inner hair cells release inducing signals such as Fgf8 that drive the differentiation of adjacent cells into pillar cells.
claims.source: Our results provide additional evidence for the notion that organ of Corti development is an iterative process proceeding in the neural-abneural direction, with inner hair cells and their associated supporting cells differentiating first, which then release inducing signals such as Fgf8 that then drive the differentiation of the adjacent cells into pillar cells.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the authors' findings and previous knowledge about Fgf8 function.

claims.claim: When Notch ligands and receptors are present in the same cell, they attenuate each other's activity, a phenomenon known as cis-inhibition.
claims.source: Previous studies suggest that when Notch ligands and receptors are present in the same cell, they attenuate each other's activity, a phenomenon known as cis-inhibition (del Alamo and Schweisguth, 2009; Becam et al., 2010; del Álamo et al., 2011; LeBon et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (del Alamo and Schweisguth, 2009; Becam et al., 2010; del Álamo et al., 2011; LeBon et al., 2014).

claims.claim: Lfng and Mfng proteins increase cis-inhibition between Notch and Delta ligands, but decrease cis-inhibition between Notch and Jagged ligands.
claims.source: Fringe proteins have been shown to modulate cis-inhibition: in vertebrates, Lfng and Mfng proteins increase cis-inhibition between Notch and Delta ligands, but decrease cis-inhibition between Notch and Jagged ligands (LeBon et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (LeBon et al., 2014).

claims.claim: The prosensory cell column adjacent to Kölliker's organ that expresses Jag1, Jag2, Dll1, Notch1, and Lfng and Mfng experiences cis-inhibition.
claims.source: We therefore predict that the prosensory cell column adjacent to Kölliker's organ that expresses Jag1, Jag2, Dll1, Notch1, and Lfng and Mfng experiences cis-inhibition (Figure 6B, red inhibitory lines), leading to only a moderate amount of Notch signal delivered to Kölliker's organ.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from known Fringe function and the authors' model shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: Loss of Lfng and Mfng is predicted to cause more cis-inhibition between Notch1 and Jag1 and Jag2, and less cis-inhibition between Notch1 and Dll1.
claims.source: Loss of Lfng and Mfng is predicted to cause more cis-inhibition between Notch1 and Jag1 and Jag2, and less cis-inhibition between Notch1 and Dll1.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from known Fringe function.

claims.claim: The entire column of cells at the boundary initially expresses early hair cell genes such as Atoh1 and Mfng.
claims.source: Our current data, previous expression studies (Chen et al., 2002; Cai et al., 2013) and previous Atoh1 lineage tracing showing inner phalangeal cells derived from Atoh1-expressing cells (Yang et al., 2010) suggests this entire column of cells initially expresses early hair cell genes such as Atoh1 and Mfng.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the authors' data and citations to previous studies (Chen et al., 2002; Cai et al., 2013; Yang et al., 2010).

claims.claim: Moderate levels of Notch signaling have been visualized at the border of the prosensory domain and Kölliker's organ in previous studies.
claims.source: The moderate level of Notch signaling delivered at the border of the prosensory domain and Kölliker's organ has been visualized in previous studies (Murata et al., 2006; Basch et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2013; Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Murata et al., 2006; Basch et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2013) and data shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: Murata and colleagues have observed Atoh1-expressing cells adjacent to cells containing activated Notch1 at the boundary of Kölliker's organ.
claims.source: Indeed, Murata and colleagues have observed Atoh1-expressing cells adjacent to cells containing activated Notch1 at the boundary of Kölliker's organ (Murata et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Murata et al., 2006).

claims.claim: The duplication of inner phalangeal cells in previous Notch pathway mutant studies was not identified due to the lack of specific markers for these cells.
claims.source: Although this phenotype can be observed in a number of previous studies in which Notch signaling was reduced or particular Notch ligands or Notch targets were mutated (Lanford et al., 1999; Zheng et al., 2000; Zine et al., 2001; Kiernan et al., 2005; Brooker et al., 2006; Tateya et al., 2011; Abdolazimi et al., 2016), the duplication of inner phalangeal cells in these studies was not identified due to the lack of specific markers for these cells.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from the authors' findings and citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: Jag1 is expressed in the cochlear duct as the first hair cells differentiate, and later in supporting cells.
claims.source: The Jag1 ligand is also expressed in the cochlear duct as the first hair cells differentiate (Figure 1C), and later in supporting cells (Morrison et al., 1999; Woods et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1C and citations to previous studies (Morrison et al., 1999; Woods et al., 2004).

claims.claim: GLAST and FABP7 are markers that label inner phalangeal cells.
claims.source: To identify the type of supporting cells beneath the inner hair cells, we used antibodies to the glutamate/aspartate transporter GLAST encoded by the Slc1a3 gene and a nervous system-specific fatty acid binding protein, FABP7, both of which label inner phalangeal cells (Furness and Lehre, 1997; Saino-Saito et al., 2010; Zilberstein et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Furness and Lehre, 1997; Saino-Saito et al., 2010; Zilberstein et al., 2012).

claims.claim: In the most apical regions of the cochlea, most EGFP-labeled cells from Lfng-CreER fate mapping are found in Kölliker's organ and very few in the inner hair cell region.
claims.source: In the most apical regions of the cochlea, we observed most EGFP-labeled cells in Kölliker's organ and very few in the inner hair cell region (Figure 2A,B; Figure 2—figure supplement 1), consistent with the expression of Lfng in this region between E12 and E14 (Morsli et al., 1998; Ohyama et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by fate mapping data shown in Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1, and citations to previous studies (Morsli et al., 1998; Ohyama et al., 2010).

claims.claim: In basal regions of the cochlea from Lfng-CreER fate mapping, many labeled Deiters' cells, some labeled inner pillar cells as well as labeled inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells are observed.
claims.source: In basal regions of the cochlea, we now observed many labeled Deiters' cells, some labeled inner pillar cells as well as labeled inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by fate mapping data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Lfng;Mfng;Rfng triple homozygous mutants show no significant difference in the number of supernumerary inner hair cells compared to Lfng;Mfng double mutant animals.
claims.source: We were unable to detect expression of the third mammalian Fringe homologue, Radical Fringe (Rfng) in the cochlea, and Lfng;Mfng;Rfng triple homozygous mutants showed no significant difference in the number of supernumerary inner hair cells compared to Lfng;Mfng double mutant animals (Figure 3B,C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3B,C.

claims.claim: Radical Fringe (Rfng) expression was not detected in the cochlea.
claims.source: We were unable to detect expression of the third mammalian Fringe homologue, Radical Fringe (Rfng) in the cochlea, and Lfng;Mfng;Rfng triple homozygous mutants showed no significant difference in the number of supernumerary inner hair cells compared to Lfng;Mfng double mutant animals (Figure 3B,C).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the authors' inability to detect Rfng expression.

claims.claim: Only Jag2 mutants show a significant increase in outer hair cells among the mutants tested.
claims.source: We found that Lfng;Mfng mutants, Jag2 mutants, Pofut1 conditional mutants and dMAML1 mutants all showed a significant increase in inner hair cells and the presence of extra inner phalangeal cells (Figure 3A,C), but we only observed an increase in outer hair cells in Jag2 mutants (Figure 3B; Lanford et al., 1999).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3B,C and a citation (Lanford et al., 1999).

claims.claim: Notch1 conditional null mutant mice produce a significant loss of lateral inhibition between hair cells and supporting cells in the cochlea.
claims.source: To test this, we examined Notch1 conditional null mutant mice which have been shown to produce a significant loss of lateral inhibition between hair cells and supporting cells in the cochlea (Kiernan et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Kiernan et al., 2005).

claims.claim: The cochlear phenotype caused by a strong Notch loss of function is due to a combination of an increase in inner hair/inner phalangeal progenitor specification and the subsequent differentiation of these ectopic progenitors exclusively into inner hair cells.
claims.source: Significantly, we saw no evidence for inner phalangeal cells in Notch1 conditional mutants on the basis of p27kip1, GLAST or FABP7 staining (Figure 3A), suggesting that the cochlear phenotype caused by a strong Notch loss of function is due to a combination of an increase in inner hair / inner phalangeal progenitor specification and the subsequent differentiation of these ectopic progenitors exclusively into inner hair cells.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from the data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: The supernumerary inner hair cells are induced at the same time as their normal counterparts when Notch signaling is reduced in the cochlea.
claims.source: These results suggest that the supernumerary inner hair cells are induced at the same time as their normal counterparts when Notch signaling is reduced in the cochlea.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from the Atoh1 expression data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The reduction in Notch signaling in Pofut1 and dnMAML1 mutants is insufficient to trigger aberrant proliferation.
claims.source: We infer from this that the reduction in Notch signaling in all our Notch pathway mutants (with the exception of Notch1 conditional mutants) is insufficient to trigger aberrant proliferation, and that our phenotype is due solely to a disruption in the boundary between the prosensory domain and Kölliker's organ.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from the EdU labeling data.

claims.claim: The phenotype in Notch pathway mutants is due solely to a disruption in the boundary between the prosensory domain and Kölliker's organ.
claims.source: We infer from this that the reduction in Notch signaling in all our Notch pathway mutants (with the exception of Notch1 conditional mutants) is insufficient to trigger aberrant proliferation, and that our phenotype is due solely to a disruption in the boundary between the prosensory domain and Kölliker's organ.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from the EdU labeling data and other experimental results.

claims.claim: Hes5 promoter contains low-affinity Rbpj binding sites.
claims.source: Indeed, low levels of Notch activation and Hes/Hey gene expression are observed at this boundary (Murata et al., 2006; Basch et al., 2011; Tateya et al., 2011) and Hes5, whose promoter contains low-affinity Rbpj binding sites (Ong et al., 2006), is up-regulated at the boundary of Kölliker's organ as hair cells differentiate (Tateya et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Ong et al., 2006).

claims.claim: Hes5 is up-regulated at the boundary of Kölliker's organ as hair cells differentiate.
claims.source: Indeed, low levels of Notch activation and Hes/Hey gene expression are observed at this boundary (Murata et al., 2006; Basch et al., 2011; Tateya et al., 2011) and Hes5, whose promoter contains low-affinity Rbpj binding sites (Ong et al., 2006), is up-regulated at the boundary of Kölliker's organ as hair cells differentiate (Tateya et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Tateya et al., 2011).

claims.claim: The Atoh1-GFP fusion protein is expressed a little later than Atoh1 mRNA.
claims.source: The Atoh1-GFP fusion protein is expressed a little later than Atoh1 mRNA (Cai et al., 2013), but also provides a reliable indicator of differentiating hair cells.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Cai et al., 2013).

claims.claim: Hair cell differentiation proceeds in a basal-apical direction over a period of several days.
claims.source: Because hair cell differentiation proceeds in a basal-apical direction over a period of several days (Chen et al., 2002; Lee et al., 2006; Cai et al., 2013), we discuss the timing of these events with respect to the basal region of the cochlea (Figure 6).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Chen et al., 2002; Lee et al., 2006; Cai et al., 2013).

claims.claim: Between E11 and E13, cells in the cochlear primordium express both Lfng and Jag1 in the presumptive Kölliker's organ and prosensory domain.
claims.source: During the outgrowth of the cochlear duct, Jag1 and Lfng are expressed in cochlear progenitor cells (Morsli et al., 1998; Ohyama et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Morsli et al., 1998; Ohyama et al., 2010).

claims.claim: Lfng activity attenuates Jag1-Notch signaling between cells.
claims.source: Lfng activity is known to attenuate Jag1-Notch signaling between cells (Hicks et al., 2000; Rana and Haltiwanger, 2011; LeBon et al., 2014) which explains why these cochlear progenitor cells have been reported to receive low amounts of Notch signal (Figure 6A; Murata et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Hicks et al., 2000; Rana and Haltiwanger, 2011; LeBon et al., 2014).

claims.claim: Cochlear progenitor cells expressing Jag1 and Lfng receive low amounts of Notch signal.
claims.source: Lfng activity is known to attenuate Jag1-Notch signaling between cells (Hicks et al., 2000; Rana and Haltiwanger, 2011; LeBon et al., 2014) which explains why these cochlear progenitor cells have been reported to receive low amounts of Notch signal (Figure 6A; Murata et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Murata et al., 2006).

claims.claim: Starting at approximately E13, the cochlear duct receives hair cell-inducing signals that reach a peak spanning the boundary of Kölliker's organ and the prosensory domain.
claims.source: We propose that starting at approximately E13, the cochlear duct receives hair cell-inducing signals that reach a peak spanning the boundary of Kölliker's organ and the prosensory domain (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the authors' model and interpretation of their data, shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: A column of prosensory cells adjacent to Kölliker's organ begins to up-regulate early hair cell genes (Atoh1, Mfng, Jag2, Dll1) in response to hair cell-inducing signals.
claims.source: In response to these hair cell-inducing signals, a column of prosensory cells adjacent to Kölliker's organ begins to up-regulate early hair cell genes (Atoh1, Mfng, Jag2, Dll1), while still maintaining expression of Notch1, Lfng and Jag1 (Figure 6B, green cell).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the authors' model and data, shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: The single column of differentiating hair cell progenitors sends Notch signals to its neighbors in Kölliker's organ that prevent them from responding to hair cell-inducing signals.
claims.source: This single column of differentiating hair cell progenitors sends Notch signals to its neighbors in Kölliker's organ that prevent them from responding to hair cell-inducing signals (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the authors' model and interpretation, shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: The column of cells expressing Lfng, Mfng, Notch1, Atoh1, Dll1, Jag1 and Jag2 will ultimately form inner hair cells and their neighboring inner phalangeal cells.
claims.source: Our Lfng-CreER fate mapping data show that this column of cells will ultimately form inner hair cells and their neighboring inner phalangeal cells (Figure 2A,B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by fate mapping data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claims.claim: The interaction between the column of differentiating hair cell progenitors and Kölliker's organ sets the boundary of the organ of Corti and establishes a single row of inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells.
claims.source: We suggest this interaction sets the boundary of the organ of Corti and establishes a single row of inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the authors' interpretation of their experimental findings.

results.result: Lfng and Mfng are transiently co-expressed at the boundary of Kölliker's organ and the prosensory domain where inner hair cells first differentiate, then diverge with Lfng restricted to supporting cells and Mfng to hair cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C6 and C52 are well-supported by in situ hybridization data (Figure 1), fluorescent in situ hybridization in Lfng-GFP mice (Figure 1B), and citations to prior work. The dynamic expression pattern is clearly documented across developmental stages and cochlear regions.

results.result: Fate mapping using Lfng-CreER mice demonstrates that Lfng-expressing cells at the prosensory domain border give rise to inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C7, C53, C79, C80, and C99 are supported by Cre-Lox fate mapping experiments (Figure 2A,B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1) showing EGFP-labeled inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells in middle turn regions, with regional variation along the apical-basal axis consistent with Lfng expression timing.

results.result: Lfng;Mfng double mutant mice show significant duplication of inner hair cells (19.5 vs 12.3 cells/100 µm) without changes in outer hair cell numbers, while single mutants show no phenotype. Rfng is not expressed in the cochlea and triple mutants show no additional phenotype.
results.evaluation: Claims C8-C11, C54, C81-C82 are supported by quantitative data (Figures 2C, 3B,C) showing specific inner hair cell duplication in double mutants but not single mutants. The lack of Rfng expression and absence of additional phenotype in triple mutants is documented, though the method for detecting Rfng expression is not fully described.

results.result: Supernumerary inner hair cells in Lfng;Mfng, Jag2, Jag1 heterozygous, Pofut1, and dnMAML1 mutants are accompanied by supernumerary inner phalangeal cells, as revealed by GLAST and FABP7 markers.
results.evaluation: Claims C12, C15, C17-C19 are supported by immunostaining data (Figures 2D, 3A) using validated markers GLAST and FABP7. The consistent observation across multiple genetic manipulations that reduce Notch signaling strengthens the conclusion.

results.result: Loss of Lfng and Mfng leads to reduced Notch signaling in the E15.5 cochlear duct, as shown by decreased N1ICD staining. Conditional deletion of Pofut1 also leads to partial reduction in Notch signaling.
results.evaluation: Claims C13 and C61 are supported by N1ICD immunostaining (Figure 4A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B). The reduction is tissue-specific (cochlea but not hindbrain in Lfng;Mfng mutants), and the partial nature of Pofut1 loss-of-function is validated by enhancement with gamma secretase inhibitors.

results.result: Jag2 mutants and Jag1 heterozygous mice show supernumerary inner hair cells, with Jag2 mutants uniquely showing increased outer hair cells among the mutants tested.
results.evaluation: Claims C14, C16, and C83 are supported by quantitative data (Figure 3A-C) and citations to prior work. The specific increase in outer hair cells only in Jag2 mutants is clearly documented and distinguishes this phenotype from other Notch pathway manipulations.

results.result: Strong disruption of Notch signaling (Notch1 conditional mutants or high-dose inhibitors) causes a very different phenotype: massive increase in both inner and outer hair cells with loss of inner phalangeal cells, indicating failure of lateral inhibition.
results.evaluation: Claims C20-C21, C56, C84-C85 are supported by data from Notch1 conditional mutants (Figure 3A) and high-dose inhibitor treatments (Figure 5A,D). The absence of GLAST/FABP7 staining in Notch1 mutants clearly distinguishes this from the moderate Notch reduction phenotype. The interpretation of combined progenitor specification and differentiation defects is reasonable.

results.result: EdU labeling shows no significant increase in proliferation of inner hair cells, inner phalangeal cells, or other organ of Corti cell types in Pofut1 and dnMAML1 mutants, except for a modest increase in border cells (66 vs 59 cells, p=0.014).
results.evaluation: Claims C22-C23, C87-C88 are supported by EdU incorporation data (Table 1, Figure 4B). The statistical analysis using a modified Wald test is appropriate. The conclusion that the phenotype is not due to aberrant proliferation is reasonable, though the modest increase in border cells warrants consideration.

results.result: Doublets of Atoh1-expressing cells are observed at the leading edge of hair cell differentiation in Pofut1 mutants, suggesting supernumerary inner hair cells are induced simultaneously with normal counterparts.
results.evaluation: Claims C24 and C86 are supported by in situ hybridization data (Figure 4—figure supplement 1). The observation of Atoh1 doublets in mutants versus single cells in controls provides temporal evidence for the boundary disruption model, though sample size is not specified.

results.result: Dose-dependent Notch inhibition in cultured cochleas shows that intermediate doses of DAPT or anti-Notch1 antibodies cause selective increase in inner hair cells with preserved inner phalangeal cells, while high doses cause increases in both hair cell types with loss of inner phalangeal cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C29 are supported by culture experiments with quantitative gene expression (Figure 5B,E) and cell counting (Figure 5C,F). The dose-response relationship and persistence of GLAST-dsRed expression at intermediate doses provide strong evidence for differential sensitivity of the two Notch-dependent processes. At least four biological replicates were performed.

results.result: Notch signaling controls two distinct fate decisions in the organ of Corti: (1) a Fringe-dependent, low-level, highly sensitive process that restricts inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells to the boundary with Kölliker's organ, and (2) a Fringe-independent, high-level, less sensitive lateral inhibition process that regulates hair cell versus supporting cell fate.
results.evaluation: Claims C46-C51 and C57 represent the authors' central model, supported by the convergence of genetic, pharmacological, and expression data. The differential sensitivity to Notch manipulation, requirement for Fringe proteins, and distinct cellular outcomes provide strong support for two qualitatively different Notch signaling processes.

results.result: Loss of Lfng alone can rescue the inner hair cell phenotype of Jag2 mutants by relieving cis-inhibition of Dll1, allowing compensatory Notch signaling.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C63 are supported by citation to prior work (Zhang et al., 2000) and mechanistic reasoning based on known Fringe function (LeBon et al., 2014). The explanation is consistent with the cis-inhibition model, though the authors did not directly test this in the current study.

results.result: Fringe proteins modulate cis-inhibition between Notch receptors and ligands: Lfng and Mfng increase cis-inhibition with Delta ligands but decrease it with Jagged ligands. The prosensory cell column expressing both Fringe proteins and multiple ligands experiences cis-inhibition, delivering moderate Notch signal to Kölliker's organ.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C72 are based on prior work (LeBon et al., 2014) and the authors' model. While the general principles of Fringe-mediated cis-inhibition are well-established, the specific prediction about the prosensory cell column (C71-C72) is speculative and not directly tested. The model is plausible but requires experimental validation.

results.result: The authors propose that hair cell-inducing signals peak at the boundary of Kölliker's organ and the prosensory domain around E13, causing a column of cells to upregulate early hair cell genes while maintaining Notch pathway components. This column sends Notch signals that prevent neighboring Kölliker's organ cells from responding to hair cell-inducing signals, establishing the organ of Corti boundary.
results.evaluation: Claims C73, C96-C98, and C100 represent a mechanistic model based on the authors' data and prior studies. While C73 is supported by expression data and lineage tracing, C96-C98 and C100 are largely speculative. The identity of hair cell-inducing signals is uncertain, and the proposed signaling interactions are inferred rather than directly demonstrated.

results.result: The organ of Corti contains inner and outer hair cells surrounded by supporting cells, bounded by inner and outer sulci. BMP signaling gradients position these domains, with inner hair cells arising first at the boundary of the prosensory domain and Kölliker's organ.
results.evaluation: Claims C30-C36 represent established background knowledge supported by citations to prior work (Kelley et al., 2009; Basch et al., 2016; Ohyama et al., 2010; Groves and Fekete, 2012). These are well-accepted facts in the field.

results.result: Background on developmental signaling: Wnt promotes hair cell differentiation, Shh inhibits it, Notch establishes boundaries between territories, and Fringe proteins modulate Notch-ligand interactions in Drosophila and vertebrates.
results.evaluation: Claims C37-C42 represent established background knowledge supported by multiple citations. These provide context for the current study and are well-accepted in the field.

results.result: Differentiating hair cells express three Notch ligands (Dll1, Dll3, Jag2), with Dll1 and Jag2 acting as conventional ligands and Dll3 acting as a cis-inhibitor.
results.evaluation: Claims C43-C45 are supported by citations to prior work. This background information is relevant to understanding the complexity of Notch signaling in the cochlea.

results.result: Pofut1 is an O-fucosyltransferase that modifies Notch receptors and ligands, generating substrate for Fringe-mediated glycosylation. Null mutants die early with Notch-like phenotypes.
results.evaluation: Claims C58-C60 represent established knowledge about Pofut1 function, supported by citations (Takeuchi and Haltiwanger, 2010; Shi and Stanley, 2003; Shi et al., 2005; Schuster-Gossler et al., 2009). This provides important context for interpreting the conditional mutant phenotype.

results.result: Background on Fringe interactions and Notch signaling complexity: Fringe genes can interact in B cell development, Notch ligand double mutants show proliferation defects, Notch signaling strength varies with receptor/ligand identity, and Hes5 mutants show supernumerary inner hair cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C67 are supported by citations to prior work. These provide relevant context for interpreting the current findings, particularly regarding Fringe interactions and the sensitivity of inner hair cell specification to Notch levels.

results.result: Inner hair cells release Fgf8 that drives differentiation of adjacent cells into pillar cells, supporting an iterative model of organ of Corti development.
results.evaluation: Claim C68 is based on the authors' findings and prior knowledge about Fgf8 function. While the role of Fgf8 in pillar cell induction is established, the authors' contribution is integrating this into their model of sequential differentiation.

results.result: Moderate Notch signaling at the prosensory-Kölliker's organ boundary has been visualized in prior studies, with Atoh1-expressing cells adjacent to N1ICD-positive cells. Hes5, which has low-affinity Rbpj binding sites, is upregulated at this boundary. Previous studies may have missed inner phalangeal cell duplication due to lack of specific markers.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C76, C89-C90 are supported by citations to prior work (Murata et al., 2006; Basch et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2013; Tateya et al., 2011; Ong et al., 2006) and the authors' data (Figure 4A). The reinterpretation of prior studies is reasonable given the new markers used here.

results.result: Technical and expression details: Jag1 is expressed in the cochlear duct and later in supporting cells; GLAST and FABP7 are validated inner phalangeal cell markers; Atoh1-GFP is expressed slightly later than Atoh1 mRNA; hair cell differentiation proceeds basally to apically; Jag1 and Lfng are co-expressed in early cochlear progenitors; Lfng attenuates Jag1-Notch signaling, explaining low Notch levels in progenitors.
results.evaluation: Claims C77-C78, C91-C95 provide technical details and expression patterns supported by the authors' data (Figure 1C) and citations to prior work. These are well-documented observations that support the main findings.
